sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: Create-time flag only. When true, allows creating this owner even though
            another owner has the same last name and postcode (same household), admitting it as a
            declared household member (which is therefore not flagged as a possible duplicate);
            otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict. It does not affect the derived
            householdId, which is deterministic. Not persisted and not returned.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            selfLink:
              title: Self link
              description: The canonical API path for this owner, '/api/owners/' followed by the
                owner's id. Derived per response.
              type: string
              example: '/api/owners/1'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: The owner's salutation, the title followed by a single space and the

content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The field is wired up the same way the codebase populates every other derived response field — an entity getter that MapStruct auto-maps by name into the generated `OwnerDto` (declared in `openapi.yml`), placed right next to `getDisplayName()`. That mechanism is fine and idiomatic. The problem is *which unit* the logic lives in.

**`getSelfLink()` is a transport/routing concern placed in the domain entity.**
- `Owner.java:565` hardcodes the REST URL namespace `"/api/owners/"` into the JPA domain model. `getDisplayName()` / `getInitials()` / salutation are genuine derivations of the owner's *own data* (name formatting) and legitimately belong on `Person`/`Owner`. `selfLink` is not owner data — it is the HTTP API's URL structure. The entity should not know how the REST layer routes to it; if the API is ever versioned (`/api/v2/owners/`) you would be editing the domain model to do it.
- This also **duplicates the literal**: `RespondWithOwnerCreated.java:17` already builds `"/api/owners/" + owner.getId()` for the `Location` header. The same path string now exists in two places, and the second copy is in the layer where it actually belongs — confirming that's the right home.

**Suggested placement:** compute `selfLink` during entity→DTO translation, where this codebase already does its REST-boundary work — `OwnerMapper` (e.g. a `@Mapping(target = "selfLink", expression = ...)` or a small default/`@AfterMapping` method, with the same `id == null` guard). That keeps the `/api/owners/` route confined to the REST layer, lets the Location-header path and the selfLink share one source, and leaves the domain entity carrying only genuine domain derivations. The `openapi.yml` schema addition itself is correct and can stay.
